verification: Geometry was read from each file's GGUF header and tensor directory, not from the publisher's config.json and not from recollection. Sizes and SHA-256 are the publisher's LFS records for the pinned commit; fetch_models.py re-hashes every byte locally before a campaign starts.
files_are_not_committed: A 4-bit GGUF is 0.4-9.5 GB. GitHub rejects files over 100 MB, release assets over 2 GB and free LFS over 1 GB, so the repository carries this manifest and each device materialises the models with fetch_models.py.
geometry_is_compared: The geometry blocks mirror the shape of profiling/model_swap/build_model.py's .geometry.json. run.py structure re-reads each local file and requires every declared field to match (STANDARD.md R2), so a substituted or re-quantised file cannot pass as the declared model.

models.purpose: Smallest dense case. Establishes the low end of the error curve without a family change.
models.notes: attn_q_norm and attn_k_norm are present (per-head QK-RMSNorm, 28 of each). Normalization is outside the timed physical block. attn_q is [1024,2048]: no interleaved gate. rope_dims is null because this GGUF does not publish rope.dimension_count.

models.purpose: Middle dense case. Same architecture and tokenizer as 0.6B and 4B, so a size trend cannot be explained by a family change.
models.notes: attn_q_norm and attn_k_norm are present (28 of each). attn_q is [2048,2048].

models.purpose: Largest dense case, and the only one with a 4:1 GQA ratio instead of 3:1, so the error curve also crosses a kv-head change.
models.notes: attn_q_norm and attn_k_norm are present (36 of each). attn_q is [2560,4096], a plain projection with no interleaved gate, unlike Qwen3.5.

models.purpose: MoE without a shared expert, 8 of 40 experts active. Tests the measured-FFN block on the sparser routing pattern.
models.notes: Read from the tensor directory, not the metadata: ffn_gate_exps [1536,512,40], ffn_down_exps [512,1536,40], ffn_gate_inp [1536,40]. There are no *_shexp tensors, so there is no shared expert and granularity is a pure top-8 of 40. attn_k/v are [1536,512], i.e. 3:1 GQA.

models.purpose: MoE with a shared expert and only 4 of 60 experts active. Contrasts with Granite on both the shared-expert and the sparsity axis at once, so one measured-block error cannot be blamed on a single routing parameter.
models.notes: MHA (16 kv heads for 16 heads), so this model exercises no GQA path. ffn_*_exps are [*,1408,60]; ffn_*_shexp are [*,5632]. The shared expert is as wide as feed_forward_length, which is why that metadata value is not the expert width here. The publisher repository carries no license tag; upstream Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B is Apache-2.0.

models.purpose: Densest routing of the three sparse models (8 of 64) without a shared expert, MHA instead of GQA, and the shortest stack (16 layers). It separates 'how many experts are selected' from 'how many exist' at a third architecture family.
models.notes: Read from this file's header and tensor directory: ffn_gate_exps [2048,1024,64], ffn_down_exps [1024,2048,64], ffn_gate_inp [2048,64]. No *_shexp tensor, so granularity is a pure top-8 of 64. attn_q/k/v/output are all [2048,2048] and attn_q_norm/attn_k_norm are [2048], i.e. per-head RMSNorm over 128 dims: MHA with QK-norm. token_embd is q4_k and output q6_k, untied. norm_topk_prob is false in the upstream config and llama.cpp's OLMoE graph passes norm_w=false, so the selected weights are not renormalized. rope_dims is null because the GGUF publishes no rope.dimension_count.
